newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares tumbled to new lows on Thursday as renewed woes on the international bullion price launched a fresh assault on the already bombed-out index, dealers said.
The price of the yellow metal dipped briefly below $340 an ounce, triggered by Belgian plans to sell gold coins, and immediately local gold stocks started to sink.

Though the bullion price recovered some ground later investors still headed out of the sector and the gold index dropped 35.4 points, or 3.23 percent, to its lowest levels since March, 1993, at 1,061.3.

Shares suffered across the board with Vaal Reefs ending off 675 cents to 243.50 rand, Kloof dropping 50 cents to 27.75 rand, Western Deep finishing down 350 cents to 113.50 rand and Amgold losing 150 cents to 293.50 rand.
"Golds have really been hit today," one dealer said.
Elsewhere in the market shares were pulled and pushed by derivatives-related trade as futures dealers head for the close-out of their near-dated contracts on Friday.
With both sellers and buyers coming into the market the picture was mixed and futures traders said it was likely to continue in that way tomorrow.
"It is going to be a quiet close-out, but there will be probably some selling (of shares) tomorrow (Friday)," one futures dealer said.

The industrials index added 1.9 points to 8,433.8 as the all-share index shed 9.0 points to 7,209.1. In the wider market there were 148 advancing shares, against 205 decliners, with 30 stocks hitting new highs and 24 stocks touching new lows.
In the futures market the June all-share contract was last at 6,472/82 from 6,439 as the industrials contract was at 7,997/8002 from 7,959. The golds contract was at 742/50 from 768.

Volumes on the stock market were a healthy 933 million rands worth with broker SBC Warburg again active in several of the bourse's big volume deals, including industrial group Bidvest Ltd, Suncrush Ltd and IBM South Africa .

Dealers said that the large trades could be linked to a massive two billion rand's worth of deals carried out on Wednesday by Warburgs involving mainly blue-chip shares moving offshore and which dealers said probably represented a portfolio being moved overseas.
"It looks like some of the shares that were sold yesterday are finding their way back into the local market," a trader said.

Other shares catching the market's eye included mining house Gencor Ltd which hit a new year high of 22.00 rand on the news of the London listing of its Billiton base metals unit. However, profit-taking saw it retrace most of the gains to end up just 20 cents at 20.95 rand.

Healthcare firm Aukland Investments rose 30 cents to 500 cents on news that a black empowerment group had bought a stake in the firm, and Delta Electrical Industries Ltd soared 60 cents to a new year high of 18.60 rand after the company said it was involved in talks concerning one of its businesses.
